rules.goal: self-play throughput (games/s and sims/s per core) in the Rust engine; actors are 64-core Zen 4/5 spot instances (znver4), the dev box a 16-thread Zen 2
rules.acceptance: keep a change only if it gains >= 3% on the benchmark (400/50 sims, 4 threads, fixed seed, python/openhex_models/ham.ctnn) with all cargo tests green; numerics bit-identical, or flagged and shown neutral by self-play (same net vs itself 50 +/- 1 over 4k games)
rules.deployment: working-tree changes only while training runs; adopt between arms via cargo test, maturin develop and infra/push.sh

cards.title: Reliable throughput benchmark (games/s, sims/s, fixed seed)
cards.hypothesis: No optimisation is believable without a stable baseline: N self-play games at 400/50 sims on 4 threads with the ham.ctnn net, reporting games/s and sims/s; plus a weak-net scenario (long games).
cards.result: Baseline (ham.ctnn, 400/50 sims, 4 threads, seed 99): 0.139-0.208 games/s/thread, 15.7k-23.4k sims/s/thread (44.6 ms/example); after the three kept changes 0.223-0.233 games/s/thread in the same 8-game run (base 0.199-0.215 back-to-back), -7% cycles. Run-to-run spread up to 1.5x from the box's learners, so A/B uses back-to-back perf stat cycles:u + the self-play checksum. Usage: cargo run --release --example selfplay_bench -- python/openhex_models/ham.ctnn [games] [threads] [seed]

measurements.what: second-net scenario, breeze.ctnn (obs 2202, 8 tensors), 8 games x 4 threads, base vs new back-to-back, 2 rounds: [cycles:u G, wall s, sims/s/thread]; checksum 246.0024 identical; games were not longer than ham's (6895 vs 6883 decisions)

cards.notes: examples/selfplay_bench.rs (actor settings: OpenHex 1v1, 400/50 sims, 2400 placement, endgame+opening branch, 1 placement fork; SelfPlayData now also reports sims and evals). Baseline, ham.ctnn, 4 threads, seed 99: 32 games 57.6 s wall = 0.139 games/s/thread, 15.7k sims/s/thread, 44.6 ms/example (3.61M sims, 3.66M evals, checksum 1206.6847); 8 games: 9.6 s, 23.4k sims/s/thread, 33.4 s user CPU (the two runs disagree by 1.5x: the box's two learners load the memory system; wall/user time vary +-5-50% run to run, so A/B is done back-to-back with perf stat cycles:u and the self-play checksum as the bit-identity check).

cards.title: Incremental / cached observation encoding per node
cards.hypothesis: Each expanded node re-encodes the full ~2200-input observation (encode + evaluate ~11% of a simulation). Caching the parent's encoding and patching the few changed fields, or encoding only the sparse diff, removes most of that.
cards.result: Kept (bit-identical, checksum 366.6948 unchanged), as a bundle with the new simd-pack-compact card. Per-node incremental patching was not done: the observation is seat-relative (the mover flips every other node) and the costly parts are derived board quantities, so those are cached instead: (1) spots-block pips from a per-map table indexed by robber tile x node (ObservationSpace::spot_pips, built once per space with the same node_pips arithmetic; for_network no longer builds 128 spaces to find the layout: layout_size), (2) road_distances for all seats cached per board in encoding::EncodeCache (key = road owners + buildings + cap + map topology, hashed, verified by compare; 8 entries round robin; mcts::Evaluator holds one and uses encode_sparse_cached everywhere), (3) the two OpenHex dice probability vectors share one deck pass (DiceDeck::probabilities_pair). Alone (3 rounds, 8 games x 4 threads): instructions 235.0G -> 229.6G (-2.3%), cycles -1.4% in the clean round (others lost to box noise), so below the 3% bar by itself; perf: road_distances 2.0% -> <0.3%, add_production 1.8% -> 0, DiceDeck::probabilities 1.2% -> base_weights 0.76%, encoding write<Sparse> 7.45% -> 7.3% (the remaining cost is the ~2200 feature puts themselves, ~5 cycles each; skipping unseated seats (encode-skip-empty-seats) would save ~80 branch-free puts, ~0.1%, so that card is not worth doing). New test cached_sparse_encoding_matches_plain (exact equality across games, maps, observers, all blocks).

measurements.what: selfplay_bench 8g x 4t, base vs encoder-only, [cycles:u G, instructions G, wall s] per round

cards.title: Allocation-free node expansion and simulation reuse
cards.hypothesis: Per-child Vec allocations, per-simulation temporaries and Game copies at chance nodes (execute_with_luck copies the game per outcome) cost malloc time (~2%) and cache misses; arena/bump allocation per search and reused buffers remove them.
cards.result: Kept (bit-identical; checksum 366.6948 at 8 games, 1206.6847 at 32 games, both unchanged). Allocations per simulation 22 -> 8 (alloc_profile, now with sampled allocation backtraces: `alloc_profile <model> <games> trace`). Removed: the per-child clone of playable_actions in Game::copy_without_history (new Game::copy_for_step: state copy only, the actions are regenerated by execute_unchecked; used by MctsPlayer::child, the shared and lock-free searches and immediate_win), the ids/results Vecs per simulation in MctsPlayer::search (the plain k=1 search now runs simulate() directly, with the root noise; the batched path is unchanged), the priors Vec per evaluation (Evaluator::evaluate returns a view of a reused buffer, softmax in place; expand_with -> expand_node taking a slice), the vec![1.0] per forced-move expansion, the three Vecs per observation in the spots/reach blocks, the Vec in DiceDeck::draw (k-th matching card by scan, same rng call), yield_resources (PerSeat), and yop_options() rebuilt on every ActionSpace::encode of a Year of Plenty (const table). Remaining per simulation: the child's Vec<Action> and the node's Vec<Edge> (pooling them would save ~2 malloc/free pairs, ~0.2%: not worth it). Alone vs the previous bundle binary: instructions 221.45G -> 218.00G (-1.6%); cycles not separable from the box noise. Whole bundle (encoder caches + pack compaction + this), final confirmation 32 games x 4 threads, 2 rounds back to back vs the HEAD baseline: cycles:u 499.5G -> 436.8G (-12.6%) and wall 33.0 -> 28.6 s in the clean round (round 1: 510.5G/42.4 s -> 515.5G/35.8 s under a contention spike), instructions 942.8G -> 874.2G (-7.3%), sims/s/thread 27.3k -> 31.6k. Not done: Game copies in execute_with_luck (per real random event, ~0.1% of the work).

measurements.what: selfplay_bench 8g x 4t, base vs full bundle, [cycles:u G, instructions G, wall s, sims/s/thread] per round

cards.title: First-layer weight format and gather layout for active inputs
cards.hypothesis: Layer::forward is ~55% of a simulation; the first layer gathers ~100 active input rows of f16 weights (F16C conversion each time). Keeping first-layer rows f32, or laying rows out for the gather / prefetching, may beat the conversion cost. Profile (perf, 8 games): Layer::forward 71.5% self, encoding ~11%, Evaluator::evaluate (ReLU compaction) 4.9%, tree ~5%, malloc ~2%. Measured per eval: 375 of 2202 inputs nonzero (spots block), hidden activity 165/165/103 of 512, policy 152 rows: ~7.5k row-tiles per eval, the first layer 40% of them. IPC 1.9-3.0: the kernel is near the FP-pipe bound (8 cvtph2ps + 8 FMA per row-tile), not purely memory-bound.
cards.indicator: benchmark delta; batched_forward_matches_single and parity (bench/parity.npz) stay bit-identical or flagged
cards.result: Layout/prefetch part done under block-major-prefetch. f32 first-layer rows shelved by analysis: the kernel is near the FP-pipe bound (8 cvtph2ps + 8 FMA per 64 outputs per row); f32 rows remove the conversions but double the weight traffic (375 active rows x 2 KB from a 4.5 MB matrix per eval), which L2 can't hold, so it would be L3-bandwidth bound; not measured.

cards.title: Cheaper legal-move generation and action-space masking
cards.hypothesis: generate_playable_actions runs at every node; the 357-slot mask fill and trade enumeration can be incremental or table-driven.

cards.title: f16 weights with F16C in nn.rs
cards.result: ~11% faster forward; log-prob error 25x smaller than torch bf16 (Nov 2).

cards.title: Register-tiled forward (compact nonzero inputs, 64-output blocks)
cards.result: single-thread eval 12 us -> 8 us, bit-identical; MCTS games 1.44x faster (Nov 2).

cards.title: Sparse observation encoder + forward_sparse in the MCTS evaluator
cards.result: ~19% on MCTS games (160 games 5.2 s -> 4.2 s), identical results; total MCTS speed-up that day ~1.77x. Sink::one_hot skipped by the sparse sink: a further ~2.5-3%.

cards.title: Batched leaf evaluation (forward_batch, union of active inputs)
cards.result: 2x per eval at 4 positions, 1.44x faster games at K=8, but no strength per time at 100 sims (virtual loss). Kept as an option (MCTS:<sims>x<batch>).

cards.title: Actor CPU utilisation: par_map chunking, background shard upload, Arc refcount contention
cards.result: actors ~33% -> ~90% CPU; fixed-board self-play 1.7x faster (one map copy per game). mimalloc was 9% slower (reverted). Shard compression preset 6 -> 1 for low-sims actors.

cards.title: Block-major f16 weight layout + software prefetch of upcoming active rows
cards.hypothesis: Weights stored per 64-output block (input-major inside), so a pass over the active rows of one block sweeps forward through one region a few lines apart; the row PREFETCH entries ahead in the nz list is prefetched (2 lines). Same FMA order: bit-identical.
cards.indicator: nn_speed us/eval; selfplay_bench checksum unchanged; cycles:u
cards.result: Kept (PF_MODE 2, PREFETCH 12). nn_speed single eval, 7 interleaved rounds: cycles/eval median 125.1k -> 117.2k (-6%), min 117.4k -> 115.5k; under memory contention from the learners up to 1.7x (200k -> 117k). Self-play 8 games x 4 threads, 3 rounds, with simd-compact: cycles:u 132.4G -> 127.9G (-3.4%), instructions +5% (prefetch address math), wall 9.2-10.2 s -> 9.15-9.23 s; checksum 366.6948 unchanged (bit-identical). Variants rejected: next-block row prefetch (+18% instr, no gain), TILE=12 blocks (register spills, +30% cycles), distances 16/24 (no gain).

cards.title: SIMD ReLU compaction (mask + bit iteration instead of a branch-free pass over 512 outputs)
cards.hypothesis: The 4 compaction passes per eval (2048 iterations) are ~5% of a simulation; comparing 8 lanes at once and visiting only set bits scales with the ~150 active entries. Same entries in the same order: bit-identical.
cards.result: Instructions per eval 229.6k -> 211.6k (-8%) with the block layout and no prefetch; included in the block-major-prefetch self-play numbers. Bit-identical.

cards.title: Lockstep batching of leaf evaluations across K independent games per thread
cards.hypothesis: forward_batch is 1.7x cheaper per position at K=4 (f16 conversion shared across positions) and cross-game batching needs no virtual loss, so every game's trajectory stays identical; the forward pass is ~72% of a simulation, so ~1.4x overall. Needs the search and the self-play loop to be resumable (state machine) or K game threads per core with a rendezvous evaluator (context-switch overhead).
cards.result: Rejected by measurement before implementing the resumable search: the 1.7x per-position gain of forward_batch at K=4 holds for consecutive positions of one game (nn_speed: 27.5 -> 17.5 us, 1.57x today), not for positions from different games. New nn_speed mode `cross` (examples/nn_speed.rs, 9 interleaved rounds, medians, 8 F-bot games at the same decision index): different boards batch 4 = 1.08x, batch 8 = 0.99x (first-layer input union 0.44 / 0.26 of the summed inputs); same board (different dice/seats) batch 4 = 1.31x, batch 8 = 1.29x (union 0.30 / 0.15). The forward is ~64% of a simulation (perf, HEAD), so lockstep over K independent games on different boards caps at ~5% before the executor/state-machine overhead and K trees per core, under the 3% bar; on an idle actor core (FP-pipe-bound rather than memory-bound) the batch kernel loses outright on low-overlap positions (per union row V cvt + S splat + V*S FMA vs 8 cvt + 8 FMA per position row). Not implemented. Next step if revisited: lockstep the same-board replays of one game (opening/endgame branches and the placement fork, ~70% of the work, kernel ceiling 1.31x at K=4 -> ~10-12% before overhead) with per-branch rng streams behind a flag (changes trajectories, needs the 4k-game neutrality check) and an async (coroutine) self-play loop so the search is resumable; the main game cannot join (it must finish first).

measurements.what: nn_speed cross mode, ham.ctnn, us per position (median of 9 interleaved rounds), single = forward_sparse_for
perf profile of selfplay_bench at HEAD (8 games x 4 threads, cycles:u self)

cards.title: Fold the board-constant inputs of the first layer into a per-board bias
cards.hypothesis: ~120 of the ~375 active inputs (ports, tile resources, numbers, probabilities, seated flags) never change during a game; summing their weight rows once per board removes ~30% of first-layer row-tiles (~12% of the forward). Changes the float summation order (not bit-identical): flag + self-play neutrality check.

cards.title: Per-robber-tile table of node production pips for the spots block
cards.hypothesis: add_production is called for every land node at every encode (1.5%); the per-node pips depend only on the robber tile, so a 19 x 54 x 5 table built with the ObservationSpace gives the same floats (same summation order per node).

cards.title: Skip the all-zero feature runs of unseated players in the encoder
cards.hypothesis: In 1v1 two of the four relative seats are empty, yet ~90 zero features are written per encode; a Sink::zeros(n) that only advances the index saves them. Identical output.

cards.title: Game::child: copy the state without cloning the playable-actions Vec that is regenerated anyway
cards.hypothesis: copy_without_history clones playable_actions and execute_unchecked immediately regenerates them; node creation (~1-2% with memmove) can skip the clone and reuse a pooled Vec.

cards.title: Policy head only for the legal moves (per-slot gather, same FMA order)
cards.hypothesis: The policy layer computes all 357 logits (152 active rows x 6 blocks = 12% of the forward) but search uses ~20. Accumulating each legal slot's logit over the active inputs in the same order (8 slots per vector, f16 weights gathered output-major) is bit-identical and scales with the legal moves.
cards.result: Kept: PolicyValueNet::forward_sparse_for + policy_subset (output-major f16 copy of the policy weights, 8 slots per vector, one FMA per active input in nz order), used by mcts::Evaluator::evaluate; new test subset_policy_matches_full passes (exact equality with the full layer for all slots). Self-play 8 games x 4 threads vs the untouched baseline binary, all three kernel changes together: cycles:u 130.7G -> 121.1G and 135.0G -> 125.6G (-7%) in the two clean rounds (a third round was hit by a contention spike), instructions 238.6G -> 235.0G, wall 9.3 s -> 8.6 s and 10.0 s -> 9.0 s; checksum 366.6948 unchanged (bit-identical). Not applied to evaluate_batch (luck accounting, 1.4% of evals) or to NetPlayer.

measurements.what: selfplay_bench 8g x 4t, base vs new (prefetch + simd-compact + legal-only policy), [cycles:u G, wall s] per round

cards.title: Wider register tiles on the znver4 actors (AVX-512: 32 registers, 16-lane f16 conversion)
cards.hypothesis: On Zen 4 the kernel could use ymm16-31 (TILE 16-24 accumulators) or zmm (half the instructions per row-tile), cutting front-end and loop overhead; the dev box (Zen 2, AVX2) cannot measure it, so it needs a cfg(target_feature = "avx512f") path benchmarked on an actor.
cards.indicator: nn_speed on an actor; bit-identical (same FMA order)
cards.result: Implemented, compiles under both feature sets, UNMEASURED (the dev box is Zen 2: the zmm path cannot run here, not even under qemu). nn.rs: module simd512 (16-lane F16: load/store/splat/fma/load_f16 = vcvtph2ps ymm->zmm) and Layer::tile_z, used by Layer::forward for every full 64-output block when cfg(target_feature = "avx512f") (on with -C target-cpu=znver4, i.e. the actor image and target-cpu=native on a Zen 4/5), otherwise tile::<8> as before: the AVX2 path is untouched and bit-identical (checksums above). tile_z keeps the block layout and the per-lane FMA order (4 accumulators, 4 conversions + 4 FMAs per weight row instead of 8 + 8, same PF_MODE 2 prefetch), so its outputs should be bit-identical to the ymm kernel; the batch, policy-subset and compaction kernels stay on ymm. Verified only that `RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=znver4" cargo build --release --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu --example selfplay_bench` (separate target dir; the --target keeps build scripts native) compiles and emits the expected loop (vcvtph2ps {sae} ymm,zmm + vfmadd213ps zmm x4, unrolled 2x by LLVM); `cargo check --all-targets` clean. Expected gain is modest: Zen 4 double-pumps 512-bit ops, so FP-pipe time is unchanged and only front-end/loop overhead halves (the kernel was near the FP bound on Zen 2). To measure on an actor (Zen 4): (1) correctness: `cargo test --release` there (batched_forward_matches_single and subset_policy_matches_full compare the zmm single path with the ymm batch/subset kernels exactly) and `python bench.py` parity vs bench/parity.npz (x86 AVX2 reference); (2) speed: `cargo run --release --example nn_speed -- bench/model.ctnn single` and selfplay_bench under perf stat, against the same build with `RUSTFLAGS="-C target-cpu=znver4 -C target-feature=-avx512f"` (zmm path compiled out), interleaved rounds. Follow-ups if it pays: a two-block tile (8 zmm accumulators, 128 outputs per pass over nz, two row streams) and a zmm batch_tile.

measurements.what: znver4 build check on the dev box

cards.title: Branch-free ReLU compaction: table-driven left-pack of 8 lanes (AVX2 permutevar8x32 + unpack)
cards.hypothesis: compact_positive (simd-compact) was still 6.4-6.8% of a simulation: its per-set-bit loop has a loop-carried chain and an unpredictable exit per vector (~150 survivors of 512, 4 passes per eval). A 256-entry table of lane permutations left-packs each vector in a fixed ~14 instructions with no branch: compare, movemask, table load, permutevar8x32 for the values, add for the indices, two unpacks and two 128-bit permutes to interleave (index, value) pairs, two stores (8 pairs always written; nz kept LANES longer), popcnt. Same entries in the same order: bit-identical.
cards.result: Kept. Bundle encoder caches + this, 3 rounds back to back vs the HEAD baseline binary (8 games x 4 threads, seed 99): cycles:u 122.36G -> 109.16G (-10.8%) and 122.90G -> 111.18G (-9.5%) in the two clean rounds (first round base hit by a contention spike: 143.8G -> 111.4G), instructions 235.00G -> 221.45G (-5.8%), wall 8.6-8.9 s -> 7.9 s, sims/s/thread 25.4-26.2k -> 28.6-28.7k; checksum 366.6948 unchanged. Attribution by difference from the encoder-only A/B: this change is about -3.5% instructions and -8% cycles (the mispredicts were the cost, not the instructions). aarch64 keeps the bit-iteration loop (same pairs). Unit test compact_positive_matches_scalar (all 256 lane masks, tails, zeros vs negatives); batched_forward_matches_single cross-checks it against gather_relu.

measurements.what: selfplay_bench 8g x 4t, base vs encoder caches + pack compaction, [cycles:u G, instructions G, wall s, sims/s/thread] per round

cards.title: Price-per-game spot fleet keeper (runs/fleet.py) replaces the Auto Scaling group
cards.hypothesis: The ASG picks pools per instance at launch and never re-prices, so a 192-core m8a metal at $1.18/h (half the per-core price of a c8a.16xlarge) is never chosen and boxes drift onto expensive pools. Actors are stateless (a shard every ~20 s), so chasing $/game across (type, AZ) pools with cheap migration is viable.
cards.result: Switched 00:07 Nov 11: old keeper stopped, group set to 0/0/0, fleet.py launched. Dry run before the switch: aim m8a.metal-48xl@1d $1.18/h ($0.85/100k games) + c8a.16xlarge@1f $0.75/h ($1.62/100k) = ~$1.93/h for ~185k games/h vs $4.26/h for 172k on the group. Rules: cheapest eligible pool per arm within the 256-vCPU quota, 3 capacity failures -> 30 min cooldown -> next pool, migrate when >20% dearer than the best pool for 15 min (one per 30 min), idle 5 min -> terminate, 14 h safety deadline. Metal per-core throughput assumed = c8a.16xlarge (unmeasured).

measurements.note: 192-core box is 24% slower per core (one process, 192 threads); linear scaling assumption corrected in fleet.json; keeper flaw fixed the same morning: an arm's share now survives 20 min without its learner (a crash had torn the fleet down)

measurements.c8g.16xlarge (Graviton 4): 60 s per 256-game shard = 15.4k games/h at $0.71-0.93/h = $4.7-6 per 100k games
measurements.note: 3.3x slower per vCPU than c8a.16xlarge; the SIMD kernels are AVX2 paths, aarch64 falls back to scalar loops. Keeper table corrected; a NEON port of the f16 tile/pack kernels would be needed before Graviton is worth using

cards.notes: A `cdk deploy` of the stack restores the group's max size to 4: set it back to 0 afterwards (runs/fleet_switch.sh does). Config runs/fleet.json (arms + shares, throughput table, caps); state runs/fleet_state.json; log runs/fleet.out. | Nov 11 10:25: Graviton detour (08:45-10:21) fixed; keeper changes: quota refusals (MaxSpotInstanceCountExceeded etc.) are not pool failures; a box over the $/game cap is replaced terminate-first toward any quiet eligible pool; arms keep their share 20 min after their learner vanishes. Observed: AWS refuses new spot launches for ~2-5 min after a termination even with vCPUs free under the quota.
